Blend and let cool for 5 minutes.
You can sprinkle a little dried mint on top.
Baked sweet potato balls
1 medium sweet potato
Peel the sweet potato, steam for 15 minutes and mash.
Once cooled, add the kashar, egg yolk and 2 spoons of breadcrumbs and knead.
Shape walnut-sized balls and roll them in the remaining breadcrumbs.
Arrange on the tray and bake for 18 minutes.
Goes very well with a yoghurt sauce.
Chicken with couscous
70 g chicken breast
Chop the chicken and carrot small.
Cook the chicken in a little olive oil for 6–7 minutes, until white.
Add the carrot, peas and water; cook for 10 minutes.
Add the couscous, turn off the heat and let it steam covered for 10 minutes.
Couscous cooks very fast; handy for dinner.
Rice and pea balls
Boil the peas for 5 minutes and mash with a fork.
Mix the rice, peas, kashar and egg.
With wet hands, shape small balls, press lightly and place on the tray.
A handy way to use up leftover rice.
Turkey and vegetable wrap
50 g boiled turkey breast
2 lettuce leaves
Shred the boiled turkey finely; chop the lettuce finely.
Spread yoghurt on the flatbread; add the turkey, carrot and lettuce.
Roll tightly and cut into 3 cm slices.
Use home-boiled turkey instead of processed deli meat.
Baked vegetable quinoa bars
Mix the quinoa, zucchini, eggs and kashar and spread 1.5 cm thick in the dish.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the centre is completely set.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut into bars.
Suitable for a preschool lunch box.
Tuna potato patties
Half a can of tuna in water
Boil the potato and mash while hot.
Drain and flake the tuna; remove any bone pieces.
Knead the potato, tuna and egg yolk; shape small patties and coat in breadcrumbs.
Arrange on the tray and bake for 18 minutes; turn halfway.
Serve with yoghurt and cucumber.
Vegetable lentil bolognese
60 g pasta
Rinse the lentils; finely grate the carrot and zucchini.
Stir the tomato paste in a little olive oil for 1 minute; add the vegetables and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the lentils and water; cook on low heat for 20 minutes, until the lentils break down and the sauce thickens.
Mix the sauce with the drained pasta.
A filling, iron-rich sauce for meat-free days.
2 days in the fridge; the sauce keeps 1 month in the freezer.
Baked cauliflower and broccoli gratin
5–6 broccoli florets
Separate the vegetables into small florets, boil for 5 minutes and drain.
Toast the flour in the butter for 1 minute; slowly add the milk and stir until thick.
Put the vegetables in a baking dish, pour over the sauce and sprinkle with kashar.
A good start for children who don't like vegetables.
Pumpkin risotto (kids)
4 tablespoons rice
2 cups hot water or unsalted chicken stock
Add the pumpkin; add the hot water a ladle at a time, waiting for it to be absorbed each time.
Cook for 20 minutes, stirring constantly, until the rice is soft and creamy.
Remove from the heat and stir in the kashar.
You can also use zucchini or peas instead of pumpkin.
Chicken vegetable stew (in a pot)
150 g chicken thigh (boneless)
Cut the chicken and vegetables into small cubes; cut the vegetables smaller than the chicken.
Cook the chicken in olive oil for 6–7 minutes, until white.
Add the vegetables and half a cup of water; cook covered on low heat for 25 minutes.
Make it as a family meal and set aside the child's portion before salting.
Homemade chicken burger (kids)
150 g minced chicken
2 small burger buns
Grate the carrot and squeeze out the juice; add the mince and breadcrumbs, knead, then wash your hands.
Shape palm-sized flat patties and place on the tray.
Fill the bun with yoghurt, the patty and lettuce.
Cut in halves or quarters and serve.
Making it at home instead of ready-made burger patties reduces salt and additives.
Cooked patties keep 2 days in the fridge; 1 month in the freezer.
Baked vegetable falafel
Pulse the chickpeas, parsley, carrot, cumin and olive oil in a food processor to a coarse sand texture.
Add the flour and mix; rest in the fridge for 10 minutes.
Serve with yoghurt and cucumber.
Baking instead of frying reduces the amount of oil.
Yoghurt chickpea salad (kids)
1 small cucumber
Remove the chickpea skins and lightly mash or halve them.
Peel the cucumber and cut into small cubes; chop the dill finely.
Mix the yoghurt and olive oil; add the chickpeas, cucumber and dill.
Whole chickpeas are a choking risk for young children; mash or halve them.
You can also serve it stuffed in pita bread.
